origin.description: Computes the inequality in a numeric vector with one of the named measures.
origin.usage:
ineq(x, parameter = NULL, type = c("Gini", "RS", "Atkinson", "Theil", "Kolm", "var",
     "square.var", "entropy"), na.rm = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. The measures are defined for non-negative values.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Parameter of the chosen measure. NULL keeps the default of that measure.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Which measure to compute: Gini, RS, Atkinson, Theil, Kolm, var, square.var, or entropy. A unique prefix is enough. Defaults to Gini.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values first. If false, any missing value makes the result missing.

origin.details: ineq dispatches to Gini, RS, Atkinson, Theil, Kolm, var.coeff, or entropy. A NULL parameter is resolved inside the chosen measure. type "var" is the coefficient of variation and "square.var" is its square.
origin.value: A single number, the inequality measure.
origin.example:
# generate vector (of incomes)
x <- c(541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261)
# compute Gini coefficient
ineq(x)
# compute Atkinson coefficient with parameter=0.5
ineq(x, parameter=0.5, type="Atkinson")

translation.description: Computes the inequality in a numeric vector with one of the named measures.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. The measures are defined for non-negative values. Missing values are NaN.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Parameter of the chosen measure. None keeps the default of that measure.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Which measure to compute. A unique prefix is enough, so "G" is Gini, "v" is var, and "s" is square.var. An unknown name raises ValueError. Defaults to Gini.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values first. If false, any missing value makes the result NaN.

translation.details: ineq dispatches to Gini, RS, Atkinson, Theil, Kolm, var_coeff, or entropy. parameter None is resolved inside Atkinson, Theil, Kolm, and entropy, so the Atkinson default stays 0.5. type follows R prefix matching.
translation.value: A single number, the inequality measure.
translation.example:
from ineq.measures import ineq

# generate vector (of incomes)
x = [541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261]
# compute Gini coefficient
print(ineq(x))
# compute Atkinson coefficient with parameter=0.5
print(ineq(x, parameter=0.5, type="Atkinson"))
